summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for recurrent bilateral lower extremity cellulitis that failed outpatient antibiotic treatment, including IM ceftriaxone. She had a history of morbid obesity, chronic venous stasis, and prior cellulitis treated with vancomycin, which was interrupted due to PICC line failure. She was started on IV vancomycin and developed mild itching during infusion, consistent with red man syndrome, managed with Benadryl and slower infusion rates. A left PICC line was placed and confirmed by chest X-ray to be in the mid SVC. Blood cultures remained negative, and her rash on the arms improved without intervention. She was discharged home with plans to complete IV vancomycin via PICC, premedication with Benadryl, and outpatient lab monitoring for vancomycin trough, Dilantin level, TSH, and creatinine. Follow-up was arranged with primary care and infectious disease to consider suppressive antibiotics.
